advance_if_all.folds: candidate has lower MAE than the reference in at least 80% of development folds (4 of 5)
advance_if_all.interval_coverage: pooled development coverage of the nominal 80% interval lies in [0.75, 0.85]
advance_if_all.player_ci: player-cluster bootstrap 95% interval of MAE(candidate) - MAE(reference) lies entirely below 0 on the development folds
advance_if_all.practical: MAE is at least 2% lower than the reference's
advance_if_all.season_ci: the 95% t-interval (k-1 d.f.) of the per-fold MAE differences lies entirely below 0
advance_if_all.team_gate: not applicable: no R9.2 target is a team-level contribution measure

amendments.change: stated which advanced candidate is served when more than one advances (lowest pooled development MAE; for the inferred output, among those that carry an ability posterior)
amendments.direction: neutral: a selection rule fixed before the evidence it selects on
amendments.reason: the pre-registration said which candidates advance but not which of several is served; fixing the rule now, from development evidence only, means the holdout cannot be used to choose
amendments.when: after the three R9.2 development runs, before any R9.2 holdout read

amendments.change: a holdout that is a RE-READ (ts_pct, already read once in R9.1) cannot raise a candidate's status above 'development_only'; it can only lower it to 'failed' if the candidate is not confirmed
amendments.reason: R9.1's baseline results on that holdout were published before R9.2's candidates were designed, so a confirmation there is not independent confirmation
amendments.when: after the three R9.2 development runs, before any R9.2 holdout read

amendments.change: an inferred (ability) record's evaluation status is capped at 'development_only' however its model's forecasts fared on the holdout
amendments.direction: more conservative: a cap applied after seeing the holdout results, and it lowers what is claimed
amendments.reason: latent ability is never observed, so 'holdout_confirmed' on an ability estimate would read as definitive validation of ability; the forecast skill of the same model is reported on the projected record instead
amendments.when: after the R9.2 holdout reads (fg3_pct, ft_pct first reads; ts_pct re-read), before any status was served

claims_not_made: that any model measures underlying ability
that results hold for seasons after 2025-26
that any candidate should be promoted
that a forecast conditional on playing is a forecast of a player's total future contribution
preregistration.confirm_on_holdout_if: pooled holdout player-cluster interval vs the development-chosen reference lies entirely below 0 and the candidate improves MAE in every holdout fold
disclosures: the 2025-26 totals CSV used to validate the shot-count reconstruction is not used in any model
the ts_pct holdout was read once in R9.1 (baselines); R9.1's ledger is loaded as a prior ledger so a second read is refused unless acknowledged
preregistration.folds: rolling origin; >= 2 training transitions; development = origins 2018-19..2022-23; locked holdout = origins 2023-24 and 2024-25 (R9.1's hard-coded split, unchanged)
preregistration.hypothesis: H1: on three-point and free-throw accuracy, an attempts-aware state-space or beta-binomial forecaster has lower out-of-time MAE than ols_history. H0 is the default: the best simple baseline stays the recommended forecaster
preregistration.multiplicity: three targets x six candidates (R9.1's eb_shrinkage, ridge_history, ridge_boxscore and R9.2's state_space, state_space_role, beta_binomial where applicable) are examined. fg3_pct and ft_pct are confirmatory: their holdout has never been read by any protocol and the hypothesis (a method that weights each season by the attempts behind it beats a regression whose slope is the same for 30 and 500 attempts) is stated here. ts_pct is exploratory: R9.1 already read its holdout (baselines only; no candidate advanced), so any ts_pct holdout read in R9.2 is a RE-READ, is recorded as one, and is weaker evidence. No correction for multiple comparisons is applied

population.evaluated: scored players who played >= 500 minutes in the target season AND, for fg3_pct and ft_pct, took >= 50 attempts of that type (same rows for every model); training uses the same rule. ts_pct: R9.1's rule unchanged
population.scored: players with >= 200 minutes over the last 3 seasons ending at the cutoff (R9.1, unchanged)
population.sensitivity: evaluation-only attempt cuts at 25 and 100 for fg3_pct and ft_pct, training unchanged
population.unit: a player-season rate on fewer than 50 attempts is not an outcome worth scoring; its sampling SD exceeds 7 points

preregistration.reference_baseline: the baseline with the lowest pooled development MAE for that target (ols_history is expected)
preregistration.selection_rule: (added as amendment 1, see below) when several candidates advance and are confirmed, the recommended forecaster is the one with the lowest pooled DEVELOPMENT MAE; the inferred (ability) output is served from the lowest-development-MAE advanced candidate that carries a posterior of ability

serving_rules.inferred: an ability estimate is served as 'experimental' only if its own next-season forecast is not worse than the reference baseline's MAE by more than 2% on the development folds AND its model-based predictive interval covered between 75% and 85% of development outcomes. Otherwise it is withheld. Meeting this is evidence of predictive validity, never a claim that ability has been measured
serving_rules.measured: served when the data-integrity checks pass (counts reconstructed and reconciled to the published rates); no model is involved
serving_rules.projected: the recommended projection is the best-validated method: a candidate only if it advanced under the rule above and was confirmed on the holdout; otherwise the reference baseline, labelled a benchmark, never an improvement
serving_rules.promotion: no R9.2 output is promoted; serving status is 'experimental' or 'benchmarked' at most (see docs/r9-2/model-safety-and-promotion.md)
